neighbours.label: degree words that mark something as openly conspicuous or strongly marked (blatant, manifest, overt, pronounced), as against subtle or mild degree words
fire: Voters were angered by the blatant lies in the campaign advertisements.
Historians see the treaty as a manifest betrayal of the smaller states.
Older patients show a more pronounced response to the drug.
Several officers were overtly hostile toward the reporters.
The editorial called the ruling a blatant attack on free speech.
There is a pronounced difference between the two dialects.
The new policy was manifestly unfair to part-time staff.
Some students openly sneered and overtly mocked the rules.

Historians see the treaty as a quiet compromise among the smaller states.
Older patients show a slower response to the drug.
Several officers were politely cautious toward the reporters.
The editorial called the ruling a careful reading of free speech law.
There is a slight difference between the two dialects.
The new policy was somewhat confusing to part-time staff.
Some students were quietly bored and rarely followed the rules.
